references.text: Abraham took the knife (מַּאֲכֶלֶת) to sacrifice his son Isaac. This is the only other place in the Bible where this specific Hebrew word for knife is used, and both instances involve a dramatic action with a knife.

Saul cut a pair of oxen into pieces and sent them throughout all the land of Israel to call the people to war. This is a very parallel action where body parts are sent to all the tribes of Israel to rouse the people to action.
Israel's response to the dismembered concubine's limbs—all the tribes gathered as one man to punish the wickedness. This shows the immediate consequence of the action described in verse 29.
Israel acknowledges that such a terrible thing has never happened before since they came up from Egypt. This is the reflection on the dreadful act in chapter 19.
The preceding context explaining how the concubine was abused and died, which led to the dramatic action in verse 29.
